# Unit test for function check_dict_case
def test_check_dict_case():
    # Empty dictionary -> False
    assert check_dict_case({}) == False

    # Single-key dictionaries
    assert check_dict_case({"a": 1}) == True
    assert check_dict_case({"A": 1}) == True

    # All lowercase keys -> True
    assert check_dict_case({"p": "pineapple", "b": "banana"}) == True
    assert check_dict_case({"apple": 1, "banana": 2, "cherry": 3}) == True

    # All uppercase keys -> True
    assert check_dict_case({"NAME": "JOHN", "AGE": "36", "CITY": "HOUSTON"}) == True
    assert check_dict_case({"APPLE": 1, "BANANA": 2}) == True

    # Mixed-case keys -> False
    assert check_dict_case({"p": "pineapple", "A": "banana", "B": "banana"}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({"a": 1, "B": 2}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({"A": 1, "b": 2}) == False

    # Non-string keys -> False
    assert check_dict_case({1: "one", 2: "two"}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({"p": "pineapple", 5: "banana", "z": "banana"}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({"a": 1, 2: "b"}) == False

    # Keys that are neither all-upper nor all-lower (title case) -> False
    assert check_dict_case({"Name": "John", "Age": "36", "City": "Houston"}) == False
    assert check_dict_case({"aB": 1}) == False
